# Compile a daily digest with MySQL

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers auto-responders work end to end across MySQL, Slack and Discord.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Gather from MySQL
3. Gather from MySQL 2
4. Blend Sources
5. Roll Up KPIs
6. Write Executive Summary (AI)
7. Google Gemini Chat Model
8. Compose HTML Report
9. Send Report via Slack
10. Sort Emails Newest First
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Cap Batch Volume
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (MySQL)
15. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing auto-responders work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Gather from MySQL → Gather from MySQL 2 → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Write Executive Summary (AI) → Google Gemini Chat Model → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Slack → Sort Emails Newest First → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (MySQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord

## Use it for

- Teams keeping MySQL and Slack aligned by hand for auto-responders
- Auto-responders work where "Gather from MySQL" is still a manual step before MySQL
- Auto-responders work that only reaches MySQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps MySQL and Slack in step for auto-responders, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed MySQL or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this auto-responders build
- The auto-responders AI step is isolated from MySQL, so models swap without touching the other 17 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Discord in the same run, for auto-responders
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 17 nodes for auto-responders before wiring MySQL

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Google AI API key; MySQL connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**Google AI API key**
aistudio.google.com/apikey → Create API key.
_Gotcha:_ Free tier is rate-limited per minute.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your auto-responders process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
auto-responders payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
